head: 0d27039965e15262308d2a1f6cc04d01da1938ab
classification_reasons: Spec is tight (R1-R13 measurable, the one flagged concern, the version, is decided), but the blast radius covers the transport every download uses (a hand-built OpenerDirector replaces build_opener), a new Windows-only runtime dependency, and a packaging contract change ([tool.setuptools] packages) that the owner's guardrail edits depend on.
The changed behaviour (no redirects, https only, datetime refusal) was not covered by existing tests; it is covered only by the 20 new regression cases. Proxy behaviour (R5) has no automated test.
Part of the acceptance (Windows clean-venv install and suite) can only be checked by the owner at this gate.
attempted: Intent: all three outcomes are addressed. Redirects are refused and come back as their status; non-https schemes are refused; a datetime start or end raises InvalidRequestError in parse_date; tzdata is declared for win32 only and packages are named so `pip install -e .` can build. Outcome 3 (the documented Setup gives a passing Windows suite) waits on the owner's guardrail PR, which plan.md and panel decision 2 name. That is by design, not a gap.

Spec/plan: the diff touches exactly the files plan.md lists (tests/test_data.py, app/data/http.py, app/data/params.py, pyproject.toml, .gitignore, plan.md). The handler list matches plan step 3 exactly, and the parse_date message matches step 2 word for word. The commit order (ff61d01 test first, then params, http, packaging) follows the Order of work. The plan.md edit records the build run's partial pip install, as the plan asked.

Claims vs code: _HTTPSHandler/_HTTPSConnection, CONNECT_TIMEOUT, READ_TIMEOUT and MAX_BODY_BYTES are unchanged. urllib_fetch's `except urllib.error.HTTPError` exists, so a 3xx goes from HTTPErrorProcessor to OpenerDirector.error('http') with no http_error_3xx handler, then to HTTPDefaultErrorHandler, raises HTTPError, and returns HttpResponse(3xx). with_retries returns any status <500 that is not 418 or 429, so a 3xx is not retried. parse_date's datetime check comes before the date branch, so plain date and string paths are unchanged.

Proxy (R5): checked ProxyHandler semantics by reading. For an https URL behind an http:// proxy, proxy_open sets the tunnel host and returns None, so _HTTPSHandler opens through _HTTPSConnection and keeps the timeouts. For http/ftp URLs with http_proxy/ftp_proxy set, the re-dispatch finds no http handler, so they are still refused with 'unknown url type' (the verifier saw this with proxies set in the sandbox). No automated test covers R5; a reviewer nit already notes this. It does not break behaviour.

Proof: test.log is literal pytest output, 89 passed (69 earlier + 20 new cases). failing-test.log shows the 20 new cases failing on main. verifier.md exercised the changed behaviour directly: each 3xx status, the Vision refusal path with one URL opened, every refused scheme, the opener's handler list, datetime refusals through make_request, clear_cache and load_klines, and the wheel metadata. The committed lint.log is red from the runner's unpinned ruff 0.17.4 (RUF100 on the noqa DTZ001 comments). Lint is the gate's deterministic check, and the owner has since pinned ruff==0.16.9 in commands.setup, so it is not a reason here.

Blast radius: callers are urllib_fetch (the loader default fetch, the CLI), make_request (load_klines, the download CLI) and clear_cache (the cache-clear CLI passes strings, so it is unaffected). The public API, cache layout and hosts are unchanged. No risk-list item is touched (deploy.action none). The diff has no guardrail files (.claude, CLAUDE.md, REVIEW.md, sdlc.yaml, policies); the sdlc.yaml pin reached this branch through the owner's PR #12 merge from main, not through the change diff.

Stale owner instruction (not a park): plan.md line 24 quotes today's commands.setup as `python -m pip install pytest ruff polars` and its replacement as `python -m pip install -e . pytest ruff`. After PR #12 the line reads `... ruff==0.16.9 polars`. The owner's follow-up edit should keep the `ruff==0.16.9` pin (`python -m pip install -e . pytest ruff==0.16.9`), or the RUF100 lint park comes back. The same applies to CLAUDE.md's Setup line. This is guidance for the owner's guardrail PR and does not affect this diff's behaviour.

Policies: security-baseline. Transport input is bounded, TLS verification is untouched (default context), the new dependency has its Risks line, and the tests open no socket (the http case targets loopback port 9, but it is refused before any connection). ux-and-brand rule 4: the new message says what happened and what to pass. data-conventions does not apply. There are no secrets or personal data in the diff.

Tests: the redirect test would fail on main even when a redirect loop ends in an HTTPError carrying the 3xx code, because it also asserts `opened == [origin]`. The scheme test fails on main for all three URLs. The datetime tests match 'not a datetime', which a TypeError cannot satisfy. The clear_cache test seeds a day file, so main reaches the comparison and fails. Pre-existing tests are not modified: the test_data.py diff adds imports and four new functions only, plus noqa comments on new lines after the owner's unlock. No existing assertion is weakened.
Skip markers: none added in the diff, and none needs a declaration in plan.md.
Drive: sdlc.yaml commands.drive is empty, so this angle does not apply.
